newsitem.title: USA: Cumberland Cty, N.C., seeks $98 mln GO referendum.
newsitem.headline: Cumberland Cty, N.C., seeks $98 mln GO referendum.

text.p: North Carolina's Cumberland County Board of Education will seek a referendum on $98 million of general obligation bonds for schools by June.
In an 8-1 vote Wednesday night, the school board decided to ask the County Commission to call the referendum.
County planners said the school system needs to spend $171 million for construction, renovation and maintenance by 2004.

The county currently qualifies for $60 million of proceeds from a statewide school bond issue, but that would rise to $73.3 million if Cumberland spends another $25 million of local money on construction by 2004. With the $98 million issue, that would be enough to fully fund its capital needs.
The bond proposal calls for five new schools, plus renovations and additions at 25 schools, and equipment and technological upgrades.
